chunks: By this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

When the time comes that Allah, Blessed and Exalted is His majesty, resurrects His servants, the days will be brought forth. The creatures will recognize them by their names and their adornments, and Friday will lead them, having a dazzling light, with the rest of the days following it as though it were a noble bride possessing dignity, being led to one of forbearance and affluence.
Then Friday will be a witness and protector for those who hastened to the Friday prayer. Then the believers will enter Paradise in accordance with the extent of their precedence to the Friday prayer.

key_terms.الجمعة: Friday (Jumu'ah) — the day of congregational prayer in Islam, considered the best day of the week
key_terms.ساطع: Dazzling/radiant — indicating Friday's special luminous status on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.شاهدا وحافظا: Witness and protector — Friday will testify on behalf of those who attended its prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the status of Friday on the Day of Resurrection according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) describes a vivid eschatological scene on the Day of Resurrection where the days of the week will be personified and brought forth before all creation. Friday is depicted as their leader, radiant with light and likened to a noble bride, serving as a witness for those who attended the Friday prayer. The hadith emphasizes that the rank of believers entering Paradise will correspond to their devotion to Friday prayer.
